assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: A taxonomy is a long-lived contract; renumbering later breaks docs and scripts.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a static scan proving every raise/throw site in the plugin carries a taxonomy code; (2) a runtime sweep triggering a sample of failures and confirming the emitted code matches the declared one. A declared taxonomy nothing raises is not a taxonomy.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_error_taxonomy.py::test_no_uncoded_error_sites
tools/plugin/tests/test_error_taxonomy.py::test_codes_are_unique_and_stable
NEGATIVE CONTROL: add an uncoded raise and assert the static scan catches it
reviewer_requirement: Reviewer confirms no code is reused for two meanings and that the numbering scheme leaves room for growth.

title: User-facing message renderer (cause, impact, exact next command)
question_or_target: Implement the renderer that turns an internal error into three user-facing lines — what happened, what it means for the user, and the exact next command — suppressing stack traces unless a debug flag is set, and never printing a secret value or a raw internal path the user cannot act on.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Message quality is judgement work; a template renderer with bad copy passes every mechanical test.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a structural check that every rendered message has all three parts non-empty; (2) a redaction check grepping rendered output for planted secret material and requiring zero hits. Structure without redaction is insufficient.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_message_renderer.py::test_three_part_structure
tools/plugin/tests/test_message_renderer.py::test_no_secret_or_stack_trace_by_default
NEGATIVE CONTROL: with --debug, the stack trace IS present, proving the suppression is conditional and not an empty branch
reviewer_requirement: Reviewer reads 10 rendered messages as a naive user and rates whether the next command is actually actionable.

title: Fail-open versus fail-closed policy table per component
question_or_target: Declare, per component, whether a failure is fail-open (hooks and advisories must never block the user) or fail-closed (validators, secret gates, signature checks must deny on error), record the rationale, and enforce the declaration with a test per component. This changes security posture and therefore needs owner sign-off on the table.
inputs: AGENTS.md#6 (block only dangerous; inject for everything else; hook errors exit 0)

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Getting a cell backwards either blocks the owner's work or ships an unenforced gate.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) fault injection into each component confirming the declared behaviour (a fail-open component still lets the operation proceed; a fail-closed one denies); (2) a static audit proving no fail-closed component has a bare except that swallows into a pass.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_failure_policy.py (one injection per component)
NEGATIVE CONTROL: flip one declaration and assert its injection test goes red
assert hooks are fail-open in every path including a syntax error in their own config
reviewer_requirement: Security reviewer independently classifies each component and reports every disagreement to the owner rather than adopting the table.

title: Degrade-loudly channel that cannot be silently swallowed
question_or_target: Implement a warning surface that survives to the user even when the calling code ignores return values: warnings are written to a durable sink, counted, and surfaced in the next health-check and at process exit — closing the 'uncontrolled silence' class where a degraded path looks identical to a healthy one.
inputs: _USER-PROMPTS.md:10983 (degrade loudly and preserve the work artifact)

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Deciding what constitutes 'loud enough' without becoming alarm fatigue is a judgement call.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a caller that deliberately discards the warning return value still produces a durable warning record on disk; (2) the health-check surfaces that record in a later, separate process. In-process observation alone would not prove durability.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_degrade_loudly.py::test_ignored_warning_still_persists
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a run with no warnings leaves an empty sink and the health-check says so explicitly (not silently)
bounded: the sink rotates and cannot grow without limit
reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must confirm the sink is bounded, since an unbounded warning log became a 774 KB pathology elsewhere on this estate.

title: CLI exit-code contract with one code per failure class
question_or_target: Define and enforce distinct process exit codes for the major failure classes (usage error, precondition failed, validation failed, permission denied, blocked-needs-owner, internal error), documented and stable, so a calling script can branch on the reason without parsing prose. Exit zero must be reserved for a verified success, never for 'finished'.
inputs: _USER-PROMPTS.md:10646 (exit code zero alone is never success)

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: A finite enumerable mapping with a per-code test.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) observed process exit codes captured from a POSIX shell; (2) the same commands run from PowerShell where `$LASTEXITCODE` semantics differ, confirming the codes survive the shell boundary intact.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_exit_codes.py (one case per class, asserting the exact integer)
CROSS-SHELL CONTROL: identical codes observed from bash and pwsh7
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a command that fails must never exit 0 even when it printed a report
reviewer_requirement: Reviewer confirms no code collides with a shell-reserved value (126, 127, 128+n).

title: Structured logging with mandatory redaction and bounded rotation
question_or_target: Implement JSON-lines logging where every record carries the error code, unit id and timestamp, where a redaction filter runs on the value side of every field before write, and where files rotate by size and count so logs cannot consume the disk.
inputs: rules/common/bash-hud-and-terminal-emit.md#2 (sanitize inside the parse, before the split)

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Redaction placement is the defect: filtering per field after a join is measurably too late.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a run that logs a planted synthetic credential produces zero matches when the log is grepped for the secret body; (2) the same log still contains the record that referenced it (proving the record was written, not dropped) — redaction that deletes the whole event is not redaction.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_log_redaction.py::test_secret_body_never_written
tools/plugin/tests/test_log_rotation.py::test_size_and_count_bounds_hold
NEGATIVE CONTROL: disable the filter and assert the secret DOES appear, proving the grep detector works
reviewer_requirement: Security reviewer must attempt a control-character injection into a log field and confirm it cannot forge a record boundary.

title: Telemetry and privacy contract: local-only by default, opt-in, no content egress
question_or_target: Implement the telemetry contract so that by default nothing leaves the machine, any future egress is opt-in with an explicit consent record, and no code path can transmit file contents, prompts, or paths outside a declared allowlist. Enabling any egress changes the privacy posture and is owner-gated.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Privacy default is the highest-consequence default in the plugin.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a static audit finding zero outbound network calls outside the allowlist module; (2) a runtime egress test with network access blocked at the OS level, asserting the full command surface still completes — if anything breaks under egress-block, something was phoning home.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_no_default_egress.py executed with egress blocked
NEGATIVE CONTROL: add a deliberate outbound call and assert BOTH the static audit and the blocked-egress run detect it
consent record is required before any opt-in path activates
reviewer_requirement: Cross-vendor security reviewer must independently run the suite under a blocked-egress sandbox; a hermetic-looking test that quietly downloads is a measured failure class on this estate.
retry_policy: two-strikes-then-pivot; never relax the allowlist to make a test pass

title: Heartbeat and progress surface for long-running lifecycle operations
question_or_target: Give every operation that can exceed 60 seconds a heartbeat with a monotonically advancing progress token, so a live-but-slow operation is distinguishable from a hung one — and document that absence of output is never itself evidence of a hang.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Extends an existing, well-specified longrun contract.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals for liveness: (1) the heartbeat token advancing; (2) an independent process-level measurement (CPU delta or output byte growth) over the same interval. The estate has proven that file mtimes alone cannot distinguish stalled from finished, so mtime is explicitly not an accepted signal.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_heartbeat.py::test_token_advances_during_a_slow_op
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a genuinely hung child must stop advancing the token AND show zero CPU delta, and the runner must report FAILED not SUCCESS
assert the longrun scripts are reused rather than reimplemented
reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must verify no code path infers 'hung' from mtime alone.

title: Runtime enforcement of declared tool permissions
question_or_target: Enforce at runtime that a plugin component may only use the tool permissions its manifest declares: an undeclared filesystem write outside the declared roots, an undeclared process spawn, or an undeclared network call must be refused and recorded, not merely documented as disallowed.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: An enforcement layer that can be bypassed is worse than none because it manufactures false assurance.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) each undeclared action is refused with a distinct code; (2) an out-of-band observation (filesystem census, process table, blocked-egress log) confirming the action genuinely did not occur — a refusal message is not proof the side effect was prevented.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_permission_enforcement.py (write outside root, spawn, network, each refused)
NEGATIVE CONTROL: the SAME actions declared in the manifest must succeed in the same run
BYPASS ATTEMPT: symlink and relative-path traversal out of the declared root must also be refused
reviewer_requirement: Cross-vendor security reviewer must attempt at least two bypasses of their own design (path traversal, TOCTOU) and record results.
retry_policy: two-strikes-then-pivot; never widen a permission to make a test pass

title: Permission-diff gate on update requiring explicit consent for widening
question_or_target: Compute the permission delta between the installed version and the candidate version and require an explicit consent action before applying an update that WIDENS permissions; a narrowing or unchanged delta proceeds silently. This is the update-time control; IMP-0059 is the runtime enforcement.
inputs: _USER-PROMPTS.md:11346 (marketplace package has malicious or excessive permissions)

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Deciding what counts as widening (a superset test over a partially ordered permission lattice) is subtle.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the computed delta for a widening pair, a narrowing pair and an unchanged pair; (2) an independent set-containment check over the raw permission sets reproducing the same three verdicts. A lattice bug shows up as the two methods disagreeing.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_permission_diff.py (widen blocks, narrow proceeds, unchanged proceeds, reordering is not widening)
NEGATIVE CONTROL: a widening disguised by reordering or renaming must still block
consent record is persisted and is version-specific, not blanket
reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must construct one widening the implementer did not model (a wildcard scope) and confirm it blocks.

title: Credential boundary: injected environment only, never a credential store read
question_or_target: Implement and statically enforce the rule that no plugin code path reads a credential file, keychain entry, or DPAPI blob: secrets arrive only as injected environment variables validated for presence at startup, and their values are never written to any artifact, log, or cache.
inputs: _USER-PROMPTS.md:10580 (secret stores or injected runtime credentials, never bundled auth files)

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Bound by the estate's absolute credential rules; must diagnose read-only and never modify a credential.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a static scan showing zero reads of known credential paths (auth.json, .credentials.json, keychain APIs); (2) a runtime file-access trace over the full command surface confirming none of those paths is opened. Neither alone is sufficient: the scan misses dynamic paths, the trace misses untaken branches.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_credential_boundary.py::test_no_credential_path_is_read
startup validation: a missing required env var produces a named error, never a silent empty string
NEGATIVE CONTROL: add a deliberate credential-file read and assert BOTH the scan and the trace detect it
reviewer_requirement: Security reviewer confirms the unit performs no rotation, revocation, or modification of any credential — read-only diagnosis only.

title: SBOM generation for the plugin's own dependency closure
question_or_target: Emit a CycloneDX SBOM describing the plugin's transitive Python and Node dependencies plus any vendored trees, produced from the lockfiles at build time and attached to the release artifact. This PRODUCES the SBOM; registry-side ingestion and querying is a separate marketplace unit.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Toolchain wiring with a schema-validation oracle.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) the SBOM validates against the CycloneDX schema; (2) its component count and names are cross-checked against an independent lockfile parse, requiring set equality. A schema-valid SBOM listing the wrong components would pass (1) alone.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_sbom.py::test_sbom_matches_lockfile_closure
NEGATIVE CONTROL: add a dependency and assert it appears in the regenerated SBOM (and that the test fails if it does not)
vendored trees present in the payload must appear as components
reviewer_requirement: Reviewer confirms vendored/unpinned content is represented, not silently omitted because it has no lockfile entry.
retry_policy: bounded retry x2 for schema-fetch network flake; a content mismatch never retries

title: Build provenance attestation binding artifact to commit and builder
question_or_target: Emit a signed in-toto-style provenance attestation stating which commit, builder identity, and build parameters produced the artifact digest, and implement verify-on-install. Signing uses an owner-held key; the unit must never create, rotate, or regenerate a key — it consumes one the owner provides.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Key handling adjacency requires the model bound by the estate's credential rules.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) signature verification succeeds against the public key for a genuine artifact; (2) verification FAILS for an artifact whose single byte was flipped after signing — the tamper case is what proves the check is live. Both must be observed in the same run.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_attestation.py::test_valid_artifact_verifies
tools/plugin/tests/test_attestation.py::test_tampered_artifact_fails_verification
NEGATIVE CONTROL: an attestation for a DIFFERENT artifact must not verify against this one
reviewer_requirement: Security reviewer confirms no private key material is written to any artifact, log, or test fixture, and that key lifecycle remains an owner action.
retry_policy: no automatic retry on a signing failure; escalate to the owner

title: Execution policy for plugin-shipped scripts
question_or_target: Define and enforce what a shipped script may do: which executables it may spawn, whether it may reach the network, which directories it may write, and what happens when it exceeds the policy. Sets the security posture for third-party-authored content and therefore requires owner sign-off.
inputs: rules/common/orchestration-patterns (Windows has no native OS-level process sandbox)

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Must honestly state the Windows sandbox limitation instead of implying containment it cannot deliver.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a policy-violating script is refused and the violation recorded; (2) an out-of-band process-table and filesystem observation confirming the forbidden side effect did not occur. The receipt must state INLINE, as a scoped limitation, exactly which containment the policy does NOT provide on Windows.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_exec_policy.py (forbidden spawn, forbidden write, forbidden network)
NEGATIVE CONTROL: an allowed script performs the same class of action successfully in the same run
HONESTY CASE: assert the documented limitation matches the tested containment (no overclaim of sandboxing)
reviewer_requirement: Cross-vendor security reviewer must attempt one escape and must explicitly grade whether the documentation overclaims containment.

title: Lazy shared MCP activation to end per-session process multiplication
question_or_target: Implement activation so an MCP server the plugin depends on is started once and shared, or started lazily on first use, instead of one stdio process per session. The measured pathology on this box was 23 sessions x 65 servers = 2,037 processes, which is the driver behind the commit-exhaustion freeze.
inputs: MEMORY: 23 sessions x 65 servers = 2037 procs; cure = shared HTTP MCP

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Live-harness change on the owner's machine with a measured freeze history.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) process-table count for the target server across N simulated sessions before and after; (2) an independent memory/commit-charge reading over the same interval. A process count that drops while commit charge does not is a sign the processes moved rather than merged.
tests_required: tools/plugin/tests/test_mcp_activation.py::test_n_sessions_yield_one_server_process
NEGATIVE CONTROL: the eager mode must reproduce N processes in the same run, proving the counter works
failure isolation: killing the shared server must degrade loudly, not hang a session
reviewer_requirement: Reviewer must confirm the shared-server failure mode is documented and that no session silently blocks on a dead shared process.
retry_policy: two-strikes-then-pivot; never resolve a hang by killing a shared service (see IMP-0066)

title: Resource-pressure guard that never terminates a live shared service
question_or_target: Implement an advisory memory/commit-pressure guard that warns, sheds optional work, and refuses to START new work under pressure — but never kills an existing process, because a kill-based guard was measured terminating a live shared service and that failure class is explicitly seeded in the regression list.
inputs: _USER-PROMPTS.md:11328 (kill-based memory guard terminates a live shared service)
MEMORY: Event 2004 commit-limit signature; memguard watchdog

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: The wrong reflex here (kill to reclaim) is the documented defect.

The second is the load-bearing one — a guard can look correct while having killed something.

tools/plugin/tests/test_pressure_guard.py::test_new_work_is_refused_under_pressure
NEGATIVE CONTROL: below threshold, new work proceeds in the same run

title: Registry storage layer with atomic writes and self-healing index rebuild
question_or_target: Implement registry persistence where every index mutation is a tmp-write plus atomic rename, and where the entire index can be rebuilt from the stored package blobs alone — so a corrupted or lost index is recoverable rather than fatal.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Atomicity and rebuild equality are exactly testable.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: a direct-write promotion path must be rejected by the guard

title: Append-only hash-chained registry event log
question_or_target: Record every publish, yank, deprecate, revoke and moderation action as an append-only event whose hash chains to its predecessor, so a silent retroactive edit of registry history is detectable by recomputing the chain.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Hash-chain verification is an exact computation.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) chain verification passes over a genuine log; (2) verification FAILS after a single-field edit to a middle record, and names that record. Detecting tampering at the right position is the claim, not merely detecting that something changed.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: an untampered log verifies clean in the same run

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Migration round-trip is mechanically verifiable.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a vN index migrates to vN+1 and back with no semantic loss (normalised comparison); (2) an old-version parser given a new-version index reports UNSUPPORTED rather than silently dropping fields — verified by comparing the parsed record count against the file's record count.

title: Publisher trust levels derived from measurement, not popularity
question_or_target: Compute a publisher trust level from measurable, auditable inputs (signed releases, conformance pass rate, advisory response time, provenance completeness) and explicitly exclude download counts, stars and ratings, per the estate's measurement-only stance on quality signals.
inputs: WORK-UNIT-CATALOG owner_questions Q9 (measurement-only ratings, no stars or download counts)

title: Detached signature format binding a package digest to a publisher key
question_or_target: Define the on-registry signature record (algorithm, digest, key id, signed timestamp, canonicalisation rules) and implement verification. This defines the FORMAT and the verify function; the trust decision built on it is IMP-0078 and the build-side attestation is IMP-0063.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: Canonicalisation mistakes are the classic signature-bypass vector.

title: Mirror conflict policy when upstream and mirror disagree

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a planted digest divergence produces a conflict record containing both digests and both sources; (2) an install of that version is refused, verified by a filesystem census showing nothing written. Recording without refusing is a half-implemented control.

reviewer_requirement: Security reviewer must confirm there is no configuration that silently makes one side authoritative.
retry_policy: no retry: a digest conflict is a security event requiring human resolution

title: Offline import with re-verification and a collision policy
question_or_target: Implement import of an offline bundle: re-verify every signature and digest against the local trust policy (never trust the bundle's own claim), and define what happens when an imported version already exists locally with a different digest — a collision must be surfaced, never silently overwritten.

assigned_model_vendor_role.rationale: An import path that trusts its input is the classic supply-chain hole.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a bundle with a tampered blob is rejected at import, naming the entry; (2) an index census before and after confirms zero entries changed on the rejected import — a partial import that then rejects is still a compromise.

title: Rate-limit-aware registry client with jittered arrival staggering
question_or_target: Implement the network client so a batch of installs staggers its arrivals, honours Retry-After, backs off exponentially with jitter, and surfaces a 429 storm as a named condition rather than as a cascade of individual failures — treating arrival rate as a scheduler input per the scaling doctrine.

evidence_requirement: TWO independent signals: (1) a deliberately mutated blob is identified by the sweep, naming the entry; (2) the sweep's coverage count equals the store's object count, proving it examined everything rather than sampling. A candidate must be unreferenced under BOTH to be deletable; disagreement means keep.
